Though the appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
2. This appeal is filed against the judgment and award dated 20.01.2021 passed by the III Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-XII, Vijayapur, in MVC No.377 of 2017.

sentences.text: 3. The claimant aged 50 years, doing agriculture work, met with an accident on 19.02.2017 and sustained grievous injures.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition before the Tribunal, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.

The Tribunal, considering the entire evidence on record, NC:
2025:KHC-K:7394 HC-KAR granted compensation of Rs.1,89,680/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realisation and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to deposit the same.

4. Aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the injured claimant has preferred this appeal, in which it is contended that, he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, but the Tribunal has taken the income at only Rs.7,000/- per month.
The doctor assessed the disability at 20% to 22%, but the Tribunal has taken only 7% and the amounts granted under other heads are meagre.

Therefore,
requested for enhancement of compensation.

5. Heard the arguments of both sides.
6.

Though the appellant stated that he was earning Rs.15,000/- per month, he has not produced any Vithal vs Javeed And Anr on 2 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19932689/
2 income proof.
Therefore, as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, as the accident is of the year 2017, his notional income is to be taken at Rs.10,250/- per month.
As per Ex.P4, he was aged 53 NC: 2025:KHC-K:7394 HC-KAR years and therefore, the multiplier was rightly taken as '11'.
The appellant has sustained fracture of right tibia and fibula.
He was admitted in the hospital from 19.02.2017 to 25.02.2017.
Operation was done on 20.02.2017 and diagnosed II L/3 tibia and fibula right and again he was admitted on 28.06.2017 for removal of screw inserted in tibia and fibula.
The doctor assessed the disability at 20% to 22% and the Tribunal has taken 1/3rd of the same as 7%.
However, as the appellant sustained two fractures to tibia and fibula, this Court finds it reasonable to take the disability as 10%.

Thus, the loss of future earnings would be:
Rs.10,250 x 12 x 11 x 10% = Rs.1,35,300/-.
7.

The appellant has produced medical bills and prescriptions under Exs.P13 and P15 to the tune of Rs.80,546/- and the Tribunal has awarded an amount of Rs.80,000/-
towards medical expenses and it needs not interference.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7394 HC-KAR 8.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 11 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
9. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of four months due to the injuries sustained.

Therefore, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.41,000/-
(Rs.10,250 x 4) for loss of income during laid up period.

10. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.80,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.1,35,300/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.41,000/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-
Total Rs.3,61,300/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.1,89,680/-
Enhancement Rs.1,71,620/-

3
The Insurance Company has already deposited the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
Thus, the appellant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,71,620/- with interest at 6% per annum and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,71,620/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
(iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
